This revision is filed against the order dated 24.11.2018 in CMP No. 3637/2018 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Payyanur.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Payyanur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It was a private complaint filed by the petitioner alleging offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The case of the petitioner is that, he purchased some land from the accused and her minor child and a release deed bearing registration No.2569/1999 was executed in favour of the company.
The accused received the sale consideration on behalf of the minor child also.
The complainant further stated that the accused made the complainant believe that she had every right to sell her minor child's rights in the property.
It is the case of the petitioner that, he is residing in the said property.
According to the revision petitioner, when the minor child attained majority, he filed a suit before the Munsiff Court, Payyanur, for partition to get his share in the property.
According to the petitioner, the accused instigated her son to file the civil suit.
Hence, the offence under 2025:KER:66566 CRL.REV.PET NO.572 OF 2021 Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code is made out in the case.

The learned Magistrate, after going through the complaint and other evidence adduced by the complainant, dismissed the complaint under Section 203 CrPC, stating that the ingredients of Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code are not made out.
Aggrieved by the same, this revision is filed.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the counsel appearing for the first respondent.
4.
This Court perused the impugned order.
Admittedly, the petitioner had purchased the property knowing that the minor had the right.
Thereafter, when the minor attained majority, he filed a suit.
In such circumstances, the offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out.
The learned Magistrate considered the matter in detail and thereafter dismissed the complaint.
It will be better to extract the relevant portion of the complaint.
" 3 Complaint was examined in this case.
He deposed before the court to the tune of the complainant.
Even according to the complainant, the suit was filed by Ismail after 13 years from getting majority.
Now the suit is filed in the year 2016.

If the accused Korokkaran Mahamood Haji vs Musaliyarakath Ayisha on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184852660/
2 had such an intention to cheat the complainant, she would have instigated her 2025:KER:66566 CRL.REV.PET NO.572 OF 2021 son to file the said suit much before.

sentences.text: The complainant had no case that the accused himself come forward and release the property to him.
On going through the entire oral evidence and allegation it is clear that the dispute arise out of property dispute the intention of complainant is to give criminal colour to the pure civil disputes.
In this matter there is no evidence to show that this accused is behind her son in the civil suit.
Being a purchaser, it is the duty of the complainant to verify whether any defect in the title deed of property.
If a complaint fail to do so, he cannot subsequently turned around and say that there is a cheating on the side of the accused.
Mere use of word of cheating in the complaint is not a sufficient ground to proceed against the accused."
I see absolutely no reason to interfere with the complaint.

There is no merit in this case, and hence,
this criminal revision petition is dismissed.
